$schema_note: VIGIL claims registry (W0-3 #398). Machine-checked by docs/tests/test_claims_registry.py, which runs in the required 'the briefing explains every agent and capability' CI job. JSON, not YAML, on purpose: the briefing-completeness job installs only pytest, so PyYAML is unavailable and the guard parses this file with the stdlib json module. See docs/claims/README.md for the schema and how to register a claim.

failure_classes.config-stated-as-code: A claim about configuration stated as a claim about code (the enforcement is conditional on how the operator has set something, but is documented as unconditional).
failure_classes.opt-in-stated-as-default: Enforcement that ships opt-in but is documented as a default that always holds.
failure_classes.display-manufactures-evidence: A display/reporting bug that manufactures evidence of a capability the code does not actually grant.
failure_classes.n-a: A straightforward, unconditional code-enforced claim not exemplifying one of the three drift classes.

claims.title: A PRESENTED capability token is validated (single-use, nine-field bound) at the external-tool executor boundary
claims.claim: The offense external-tool executor (run_external_tool), WHEN a capability token is presented, validates it immediately before launching the tool — nine-field-bound (deployment/engagement/operation-hash/normalized target/tool/danger class/…), single-use, owner-signed — and burns its nonce in the existing O_EXCL nonce ledger, so a presented authorization cannot be stale, replayed, or reused for a different operation by the time execution happens. Enforcement is OPT-IN at this stage: a call with no token still runs (capability=None is not yet a refusal), and minting a token at the sovereign approval leg + threading it through every production caller — so a production deployment REQUIRES one on every run — is named follow-on work in the decision doc.

claims.title: Engagement log rotates with retention (no silent discard)
claims.claim: The engagement log rotates through a numbered backup ring and retains history up to an explicit retention window, rather than discarding it in place.

claims.title: Concurrent engagements do not cross-log (per-context slug)
claims.claim: The bound engagement slug is held per execution context, so two concurrent engagements in one process write to separate log files instead of cross-logging.

claims.title: Live directory resolves absolute and CWD-independent
claims.claim: The default live directory resolves to an absolute path anchored to the CRUCIBLE root, so it is the same store regardless of the current working directory.

claims.title: Blackboard SQLite corruption detected at open
claims.claim: The blackboard SQLite store runs an integrity check on open and raises a clear error when the store is corrupt or not a database.

claims.title: vigil doctor and sigil doctor share ONE check registry (no drift; README block CI-regenerated)
claims.claim: `vigil doctor` and `sigil doctor` share ONE check registry in `vigil_core.doctor` — the same `REQUIRED_CONTROLS` production-posture spec, the same fail-closed, opt-in gate decision (`evaluate`), and the same exit roll-up (`overall_ok`) — so the two entry points can never drift on which controls are required, what counts as satisfied, or whether a failure flips the exit code; and the security-posture block documented in README.md is REGENERATED from that registry by a required CI guard, not authored by hand, so it cannot rot.
